Updates and Fixes

Development log

5. May 2025

  • Combat and combat handlers

    • Health regeneration
    • Mana regeneration
    • Enter/Leave combat
    • TakeDamage: Takes parry and defence into consideration(parry is calculated by level difference and is not an attribute.)
    • Respawn timer: respawn time for players, making sure there is a brief moment where players can tell they have died.

  • Pixel movement

    • mob.Step() Changes to DM's step() behaviour, to create a more fluent movement. It takes client input times and world-time into consideration.
    • atom/movable.Bump() There are a few miniscule behaviour-changes to Bump()

  • Client keyboard input

    • client.Movement() reads from key inputs and determines movement direction pr server tick.
    • Using one of BYOND's new... or not so new macro function Any-key. Client registers keyboard input at real-time, processed pr server tick.
    • Future development updates will focus on keyboard mapping, creating Actionbar shortcuts so players can bind abilities to specific keys.

  • Kill reward fundamentals

    • Monsters rewards stats and experience on kill
    • Specific monster types rewards it's own specific stats(i.e: some reward reiatsu-based stats, some defence etc...)

  • Monster behaviour

    Most of the old Bleach games found on BYOND, based on SoC's source code, is known for bad behavioural mobs. Those old behaviours will never exist in this game. Avoiding large server-side processing, implementing smart, collition-based player detection and AI rest model, mobs will only be actively ready to trigger it's behaviour when players are nearby.

    • AI Controller model makes sure mobs have a stable behaviour foundation that is easy to expand upon for future content.
    • AI Trigger is a collition-based trigger that doesn't need to actively scan for players. It only triggers at the event of a player entering it's vicinity.

  • Leveling and Experience

    • Players get experience and rewards by killing monsters. Higher leveled monsters rewards more experience.
    • Dummy training is unfortunately still a thing. Though I hate to admit it, it was a key component to this style of game, though it will only act as a form of introductory experience gain. It's
